relevance_note: Single-patient case report of an 8-year-old girl with a NOD2 variant: "identifying a de novo pathogenic variant in the NOD2 gene (c.1807C > A NM_022162; p.H603N NP_071445), confirming the diagnosis".
method_note: Read the paper in full; JSON assembled by a short Python script from values chosen by reading. Table 1 is a generic diagnostic-criteria table, not patient data. Inheritance left 'not reported' and parental_testing_statement 'not reported': the paper calls the variant 'de novo' but never states that the parents were tested (rule 8 / D-24). Zygosity and variant type not stated for the variant (only generic 'autosomal dominant' and 'gain-of-function (GOF) mutations in NOD2' in the Introduction), so 'not reported'. Cytokine and transcriptomic results are patient-level, not a functional assay of the variant, so functional_evidence_statement is 'not reported'. Age at last evaluation recorded as the age at referral ('8-year-old'); follow-up continued one month after discharge without a new age. Age at diagnosis not stated as an age. Time-specific statements not recorded as exclusions to avoid false contradictions: 'was afebrile' and 'with no joint limitations' at the first examination, followed 15 days later by fever and functional limitation (recorded as observed). Checklist 'arthritis or joint synovitis' left 'not reported': arthritis is explicitly absent but synovitis is not separately addressed (synovial hypertrophy is described around tendons only). 'hepatomegaly or hepatic granulomas' left 'not reported' (no hepatosplenomegaly excludes hepatomegaly but not hepatic granulomas); splenomegaly marked excluded from 'no signs of hepatosplenomegaly'. Normal ophthalmological examination, echocardiography and urinalysis recorded as whole examinations (D-27) and not used to exclude cataract, glaucoma, pericarditis or nephritis. Vital status not explicitly stated. No internal contradictions found.
